title: Configurable editorial compliance engine
description:
# Limatus: configurable editorial compliance engine


Durable vision page: Limatus wiki `project/wiki/editorial-compliance-engine.md`.

## Intent

As a **publication's editorial team**, I want Limatus to enforce *our* editorial policies — supplied by our CMS at request time — using deterministic scans and a zero-shot decision model, and to suggest rewrites only when asked, so editors see every policy problem marked on the draft and stay in control of what changes.

First integration: **Papyrus CMS** (Papyrus initiative **PPY-ed678d** "Limatus editorial checks in Papyrus": epics PPY-4f539b storage/plugin/Lambda, PPY-8473b0 admin panel, PPY-95f751 copy-editing component, PPY-0233f1 feedback capture).

## Product shape

- **Policy pack, not style profile.** A versioned set of policies plus settings, sent by the caller with each request; Limatus is stateless. Each policy: `id, version, title, guidance, severity (info|warn|error), enabled, detectors[], examples{violates[],complies[]}, rewriteGuidance`. Existing `style-profile.yml` files become an import path.
- **Three lanes:**
  - **Rules** (deterministic/NLP): existing always-lane checks + regex/lexicon/phrase detectors as policies; built-in "AI-writing tells" pack ported from avoid-ai-writing (MIT, attribute); optional NLP extra (e.g. spaCy).
  - **Classifier** (Jev, TypeSafe System One): per-segment requests at sentence, paragraph and document scope, all applicable questions batched in one request; sentence state = `{target, paragraph}`; cache by fingerprint(question set) + hash(segment text); `reviewBand` until calibrated.
  - **Suggestions** (OpenAI `gpt-6-luna`): on-demand `suggest(finding)` → 2–3 options, no fabricated facts. **Never used to find problems**; the OpenAI judge lane is removed.
- **Output: standoff annotation.** `segments[]` (paragraph/sentence ids + offsets), `findings[]` (policyId, policyVersion, lane, segmentId, span, severity, probability, status violation|review, message, evidence), `coverage[]` (per segment × policy probabilities, including passes). Offsets in **UTF-16 code units**; finding ids stable across rescans (hash of policy + normalized segment text). Markus directive rendering stays as an optional output.
- **Entry points:** `check(request) -> result`, `suggest(request) -> options`; JSON Schemas published by Limatus are the contract.
- **Feedback:** editor dismiss/accept → labels → per-policy calibration (isotonic), retrieved few-shot examples, offline Jev-Flywheel question steering.

## Epic order

1. Contracts + Markus-aware segmenter (unblocks Papyrus work)
2. Rules lane on policies + AI-tells pack
3. Jev classifier lane
4. Luna suggestions; retire judge from scan
5. Feedback labels and calibration

## Decisions (2026-10-19)

1. **Luna may assist policy authoring:** it drafts atomic Jev questions from an editor's prose guideline; the editor approves before the detector is saved. Luna still never runs in the scan path.
2. **No publish gate:** findings are advisory; `block` severity shows a warning at publish time but does not stop publishing. (Severity scale becomes `info|warn|error` to avoid implying a gate.)
3. **CodeMirror 6** replaces the body `<Textarea>` in the Papyrus article editor.
4. **No backward compatibility required:** redesign the CLI/SDK for the most elegant system; the `scan → decide → options → apply` loop, the OpenAI judge lane, and the `papyrus editorial` wrapper may be replaced.
5. **Selection rewrites:** editors can ask for rewrite options on any selected sentence or paragraph, not only on findings.

## References

- avoid-ai-writing: https://github.com/conorbronsdon/avoid-ai-writing
- Jev client template: `~/Projects/Jev-Flywheel/jev_flywheel/jev.py`; calibration: `~/Projects/Jev-Calibration/README.md`
- Luna LiteLLM quirks (max_completion_tokens, no temperature): `~/Projects/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/src/decision_flywheel_evaluations/unified_openai.py`
